title: PSI says its AI proved a quantum conjecture — with limits written down
summary: Physical Superintelligence says an internal system running an unreleased Anthropic model proved the Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture in three days, Lean-checked, and lists exactly what that check does not cover. Then OpenAI's Pando, the Git backend it built when Codex agents overwhelmed its monorepo, and a week in review about how few people are doing the checking.

topics: PSI's proof of the Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture (announced 6 November 2026): internal research system using instances of a non-public Anthropic model found a complete proof on day three of a run, then improved the bound twice; influence >= (8*sqrt15/(125*pi^4))*eps^(5/2)/d^6 >= (eps/d)^7; Lean 4.33 formalization replayed through the kernel, lean4lean and comparator/nanoda, with a control showing a build can accept a false statement; trust boundary: the statement (PrintedConjecture, in a Mathlib-only file) is for a reader to confirm, the paper is not machine-checked; one improved-constant theorem assumes Agarwal–Ben-David unformalized; David Turturean built the system and is responsible for correctness; Jim Halverson audited; Stanford's Blanc, Docter, Strassle and Tan reading and writing an exposition; follows Lovett–Zhang plan, links to Reimer's Butterfly Lemma; counts queries not running time; no public Aaronson verdict as of recording

OpenAI's Pando Git backend (post 2 November 2026 by Aaron Friel, Taylor Blau, Ted Nyman; read via secondary write-ups): Codex-driven load made monorepo fetches/pushes slow and reliability at times below 90%; kept Git protocol and client, replaced the server layer; packs streamed to blob storage, per-ref compare-and-swap in a metadata store, packfile-URIs reads from regional caches (>99% hit), LSM-style pack tiering; median push latency down ~80%, ~1 PB/day, 57 TB peak hour; production since April 2026; trade-offs: no cross-branch snapshot, trunk-only advertisement (millions of branches); built in 10 weeks, one engineer plus agent teams, Rust, Lean and TLA+ specs; internal only; contrasted with Anthropic's Scion (left Git, no merge queue)

Week in review, 2–8 November 2026: data-center ballot measures and the Nov 5 selloff (permits vs leverage still unresolved), and the week's counts of human checkers — Observer's 12–60 OpenAI reviewers, 61 of 948 kernel LPEs patched, METR's 2.5 FTE with redacted evidence, four Stanford readers — against FlashProve's 70–95x cost of mechanical checking

dives.story: OpenAI's Pando: keeping Git under agent load
dives.why_it_matters: Platform and developer-productivity teams whose repos are filling with agent branches get the second lab's design for the same bottleneck, and a concrete keep-Git-or-leave-it choice against Anthropic's Scion.

lore.note: On version control under agent load, Ada staked out 'keep Git': throwing out the protocol throws out the ecosystem and every agent trained on it. Alan was unsure, arguing Scion's dropped merge queue questions the old workflow itself while Pando only makes it fast. Unresolved.
